claims.statement: Rose from the northern steppe and united his people; governed through myriarchs (commanders of ten thousand households) and judges (duanshiguan), entrusting power to only a few kinsmen and favoured ministers.
Appointed the Guowang as Grand Preceptor.
After taking the Central Plain, set up the Tax Commissions of the Ten Circuits and employed Confucian scholars.
On his accession established the Three Dukes (dates of appointments unknown).
Filled the post of Director of the Secretariat with a chief minister; first appointed one Right and one Left Chancellor.
On accession promoted veteran officials, renewed institutions, set court ritual, built the capital, and had Liu Bingzhong and Xu Heng define the offices.
Left the Three Dukes mostly vacant, appointing only a Grand Protector; had the crown prince concurrently hold the Directorship of the Secretariat.
Appointed a single Chancellor and two Administrators of Affairs.
Appointed one Left and one Right Vice-Director of the Secretariat.
Commissioned by Shizu to weigh ancient and modern precedent and fix the offices at court and in the provinces.

unresolvedReferences.description: The Guowang made Grand Preceptor in Taizu 12 is identified only by title in this chapter.
The crown princes of Dade 11 and Yanyou 3 are not named; recorded as separate title-identified persons, and neither is identified with Shizu's crown prince.
The text says Taizu allotted the households to 旭烈大王; if this is Hülegü (Taizu's grandson), the attribution to Taizu is chronologically doubtful. Identity with Hülegü is not stated in the text.
哈贊大王, 阿八合大王 (s0589) and 哈兒班答大王 (s0592) are probably the Ilkhans Ghazan, Abaqa and Öljeitü, but the chapter gives no identification or kinship; no family edges asserted.
別吉大營盤 ('the Beki's great encampment', also s0849): the beki (princess) is unnamed; possibly Sorghaghtani Beki, not asserted.
阿難答王 is probably Ananda, Prince of Anxi (grandson of Shizu), but the chapter gives no identification, kinship or date; the Western bound is inferred only from the Daidu office name.
中山察魯局 (Zhongshan Chalu Bureau): 察魯 may be a personal name (an eponym like 劉元帥 and 趙良 nearby) or a place/ethnonym; not linked as a person.
宣德八魯局 (Xuande Balu Bureau): 八魯 may be an eponym or a place/ethnonym; not linked as a person.
